candidates.exact_span:
Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb)
                                                   unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether concentrations are treated as ug/l/ppb or another parameter-specific unit changes the numeric value used when comparing reported measurements to enforceable limits.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When DL exceeds MQL, substituting one-half DL versus treating the result as non-numeric or missing changes the effluent value used for limit comparison (A) and whether the case is classified as a usable numeric result versus a no-data/missing-evidence state (C).

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating sub-MQL detections as 'no data inputted' removes a numeric basis for compliance comparison (A) and shifts classification among documented no-data, conditional non-requirement, and unresolved missing-evidence states (C).

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The permissive 'either ... or "0"' choice yields different numeric inputs for limit comparison (A) and different semantics for whether a reported-but-below-MQL value constitutes adequate evidence versus an effective zero/no-result state (C).

The instream waste concentration formula determines the calculated concentration against which water-quality-based numeric limits may be evaluated; different readings of its terms or constants change whether a measurement is treated as exceeding an applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: F    = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is a direct input to the instream concentration calculation; a different authorized or applied F value changes the computed concentration and thus limit-exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting 4Q3 versus harmonic mean as Qa changes the calculated instream concentration and applicable limit comparison (A); which flow statistic is required also bears on whether flow-related monitoring obligations were applicable (B).

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS is taken from the receiving stream or from effluent on intermittent streams changes partition-coefficient-based dissolved-criteria calculations (A) and which monitoring source was required for that parameter (B).
This conversion from dissolved criteria (Cr) to total-metal criteria (Ct) determines the enforceable numeric limit form applied when comparing total-metal effluent measurements.

candidates.locator: page 2, section body, Stream Linear Partition Coefficient table
candidates.computation_change_reason: The tabulated Kpo, alpha, Kp, C/Ct, and dissolved value (here shown as 0) govern conversion to an applicable total-metal limit; interpreting a zero or blank dissolved value differently changes the numeric limit used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable acute aluminum criterion switches to a fixed 750 ug/l when stream pH is below 6.5 (A); whether pH must be monitored to establish that condition affects monitoring-obligation applicability (B).

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable chronic aluminum criterion switches to a fixed 87 ug/l when stream pH is below 6.5 (A); establishing that pH threshold may require pH monitoring whose applicability is evaluated under B.

The hardness-dependent cadmium acute correction factor directly scales the numeric acute criterion (A); hardness measurement may be required to apply it, affecting monitoring-obligation determination (B).
The hardness-dependent cadmium chronic correction factor directly scales the numeric chronic criterion (A); whether hardness monitoring was required to compute the applicable limit bears on B.
